title: The different levels of post-school qualifications in Australia and the proportion...
prompt: The chart below shows the different levels of post-school qualifications in Australia and the proportion of men and women who held them in 1999. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features and make comparisons where relevant.
guideHtml:
HƯỚNG DẪN VIẾT NHANH (Task 1 – Bar chart)

1. Hiểu đề

Biểu đồ so sánh tỷ lệ nam và nữ có các loại bằng cấp sau phổ thông tại Úc năm 1999: Skilled vocational diploma; Undergraduate diploma; Bachelor’s degree; Postgraduate diploma; Master’s degree

Dạng: so sánh giữa 2 nhóm (male vs female)

2. Introduction

The bar chart compares the proportions of males and females holding different post-school qualifications in Australia in 1999.

3. Overview

  • Nam chiếm đa số ở hầu hết các bậc
  • Ngoại lệ: Undergraduate diploma → nữ cao hơn
  • Chênh lệch lớn nhất: Skilled vocational diploma & Postgraduate diploma
  • Bachelor’s degree gần như cân bằng

4. Body 1 – Nam cao hơn

  • Skilled vocational diploma: nam \~90% vs nữ \~10% (chênh cực lớn)
  • Postgraduate diploma: \~70% vs \~30%
  • Master’s degree: \~60% vs \~40%
  • Bachelor’s degree: \~55% vs \~45% (gần ngang)

→ xu hướng: nam chiếm ưu thế ở trình độ cao và nghề

5. Body 2 – Nữ cao hơn

  • Undergraduate diploma: nữ \~70% vs nam \~35%

→ đây là điểm nổi bật duy nhất
sampleHtml:
The bar chart compares the proportions of men and women holding different post-school qualifications in Australia in 1999.

Overall, men dominated vocational and postgraduate qualifications, while women were more represented in undergraduate and bachelor’s degrees.

Men accounted for a very high share in skilled vocational diplomas (about 90%), compared to only around 10% of women. A similar pattern is seen in postgraduate diplomas (around 70% men vs 30% women) and master’s degrees (60% vs 40%).

In contrast, women outnumbered men in undergraduate diplomas, making up about 70% compared to roughly 35% of men. For bachelor’s degrees, women also had a slightly higher proportion (around 50%) than men (about 45%).
chartDescription:
TYPE: bar chart
TITLE: Post-School Qualifications in Australia 1999
UNITS/AXES: X-axis: Percentage (0% to 100% in 10% increments); Y-axis: Qualification Type
SERIES/CATEGORIES:
Qualifications: Skilled Vocational Diploma, Undergraduate Diploma, Bachelor's Degree, Postgraduate Diploma, Masters Degree
Gender: Female, Male
DATA:
Skilled Vocational Diploma: Female ≈10%, Male ≈90%
Undergraduate Diploma: Female ≈70%, Male ≈35%
Bachelor's Degree: Female ≈45%, Male ≈70%
Postgraduate Diploma: Female ≈30%, Male ≈70%
Masters Degree: Female ≈40%, Male ≈60%
KEY FEATURES:
*   Males had a significantly higher percentage in Skilled Vocational Diplomas (≈90%) compared to females (≈10%).
*   Females had a much higher percentage in Undergraduate Diplomas (≈70%) than males (≈35%).
*   Males had a higher percentage in Bachelor's Degrees (≈70%) and Postgraduate Diplomas (≈70%) compared to females (≈45% and ≈30% respectively).
*   For Masters Degrees, males (≈60%) still outnumbered females (≈40%), but the gap was smaller than for Skilled Vocational, Bachelor's, and Postgraduate Diplomas.
*   The highest qualification rate for females was in Undergraduate Diplomas (≈70%).
*   The highest qualification rate for males was in Skilled Vocational Diplomas, Bachelor's Degrees, and Postgraduate Diplomas (all ≈70-90%).
